$comment: Copy to ./odw.config.json, ~/.config/odw/config.json, or pass --config. All keys are TOP-LEVEL (no 'settings' wrapper; odw warns about unknown or misplaced keys). odw never calls model APIs directly: each adapter is a local CLI it shells out to. The nine below ship as built-ins, so you only need this file to change defaults, tune flags, or add your own adapter.
//stallTimeout: ODW extension. Seconds an agent may print nothing on stdout or stderr before it is killed (like a timeout) and restarted, at most stallRestarts times per agent call; null (the default) turns the watchdog off. It stays off for every built-in adapter because some CLIs (gemini, qwen, kimi in text mode) print nothing until they finish: enable it for adapters that stream progress — claude (stream-json: an event per turn), codex (exec --json: an event per item), kilo, opencode — with a value above the longest single tool call. An adapter's own "stallTimeout" overrides this value; 0 turns the watchdog off for that adapter.
//transientRetries: ODW extension. A failed agent is classified from its CLI's exit status and output: rate_limit, quota, auth, timeout, stalled, not_found, permission or exit. A rate-limited one is run again after a backoff (the retry-after its CLI printed, else 15s doubling per retry, plus up to 20% jitter), at most transientRetries times per agent call and never waiting more than maxBackoff seconds at once. A spent quota or a failed login is never retried: its error says what to do, and the run goes on. An adapter's own "failures" patterns (regular expressions per class: rate_limit, quota, auth) are matched before the built-in table.
//worktreeSetup: ODW extension. A command run in every new isolated worktree (agent(…, { isolation: "worktree" })) once .worktreeinclude has brought files in, before the agent starts: a string runs through the platform shell, an array as an argv without one. It runs in the agent's workspace with ODW_RUN_ID, ODW_AGENT_ID and ODW_PORT set, and is killed after worktreeSetupTimeout seconds; one that fails or times out fails that agent (not the run), quoting the end of its output. null (the default) runs nothing.
//worktreeTeardown: ODW extension. A command run in an isolated agent's workspace just before its worktree is removed — after the agent finished, failed or was stopped, and after a failed setup — with the same variables as worktreeSetup, plus ODW_SLOT (odw-<run>-<agent>, also the default COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME): e.g. "docker compose down -v". Killed after worktreeTeardownTimeout seconds; a failure is logged, the agent's result stands. null (the default) runs nothing.
//portRange: ODW extension. Every agent process gets ODW_PORT: a port from this inclusive range that no other running agent of the run holds (ports something already listens on are passed over), kept until its call settles, so a workflow can say "start your dev server on $ODW_PORT". Keep the range wider than concurrency.
//fanOutWarn: ODW extension. When one parallel() or pipeline() call fans out more than this many tasks or items, the run logs one warning with the count (it never blocks); 0 or null turns it off. What a run spends — tokens and cost as adapters report them (the built-in claude does; codex reports tokens, no cost), else output tokens estimated as chars/4 — shows in odw status, the live view and the dashboard.
//adaptiveConcurrency: ODW extension. An adapter's own "concurrency" (my_wrapper below sets 2) caps how many of its agents run at once, inside the run-wide concurrency (an agent needs a slot in both; each adapter queues first come, first served, and a throttled adapter never holds up the others). With adaptiveConcurrency, a rate limit halves its adapter's cap — that of an adapter without one starts at the run-wide cap — for the rest of the run, never below 1, and each minute without another gives one slot back; both are logged. false keeps every cap fixed. odw doctor and odw run's start banner show the caps.
//staggerFanOut: ODW extension. On adapters that declare "promptCache": true (the built-in claude does), one parallel() or pipeline() call whose agents' prompts share at least their first 1024 characters starts `first` of them, and the rest once the first one's CLI has produced output or delayMs later, whichever is sooner — so they read the prefix from the prompt cache instead of each paying for it. A lone agent, an agent with a shorter or different prompt, and a replayed one never wait; a stop ends the wait at once; each staggered fan-out logs one line. false or null turns it off.
//maxDiffBytes: ODW extension. An agent that runs with isolation: "worktree" leaves what it changed as a unified diff in the run directory (agents/<agentId>.diff): odw diff prints it, odw apply applies it, and the dashboard's Changes tab shows it. Past maxDiffBytes the diff keeps its head, cut at a line, and a note; its counts still describe the whole change. keepBranches also commits every isolated agent's change to a branch odw/<runId>/<agentId>-<label> of the source repository (keep: true does that for one agent; keep: false opts one out).
//applyVerify: ODW extension. A command line odw apply runs at the repository root after each apply, through the shell and within "timeout" — e.g. "npm test". When it fails, times out or is interrupted, that apply is rolled back exactly: the paths the diff touched get back their content and index entries, and nothing else is touched (no stash, no reset). odw apply --verify "<cmd>" overrides it for one apply, --no-verify skips it, --check never runs it. null (the default): no command.
//maxTranscriptBytes: ODW extension. While each agent runs, what its CLI prints is kept in the run directory as its transcript: agents/<agentId>.transcript.jsonl (a JSONL adapter's events as received, other adapters' output as text lines) and agents/<agentId>.stderr.txt (the end of its stderr). odw logs <run> --agent <id|label> prints it readably (--raw as kept, --follow while it runs). Past maxTranscriptBytes per agent one truncation line ends it; 0 keeps no transcripts.
//recordVersions: ODW extension. What each run ran with, for odw compare: on an adapter's first agent of the run, `<cli> --version` (its command's first argv element) runs beside the agent, killed after 3s, and lands as a cli_version event (odw status and the API show it). It never delays or fails the run; a CLI that does not answer is recorded as unknown. Adapters whose command is node (or another interpreter), a script or a relative path are not probed. false runs no probe; the odw version and the workflow's sha256 in meta.json, and the settings on run_started, are recorded either way.
//permissions: ODW extension. What the run's agents may do: "read" (look, never edit or run commands — for research and review fan-outs), "edit" (the default: what every built-in always ran with) or "full" (no sandbox, no approvals). odw run|rerun|resume --permissions overrides it per run; an adapter's own "permissions" and an agent()'s { permissions } may only lower it. Each adapter's flags per tier are its "permissionArgs", spliced where its command has "{permission_args}". An agent that asks a CLI with no read flags for "read" fails before it starts; one that asks for "full" where the CLI declares none runs with its "edit" flags, logged once. To cap one built-in without redefining it, give only the fields you change: "adapters": { "codex": { "permissions": "read" } }.
//trust: ODW extension. "untrusted" (or odw run|rerun|resume --untrusted) is for someone else's repository: its CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, hooks, MCP servers and settings would steer or run inside every agent. Each adapter's "untrustedArgs" go after its tier's flags (claude --safe-mode, qwen --safe-mode; omp keeps out extensions, skills and rules only); a CLI with no documented way to ignore the repository is said once per run (its "untrustedNote"), never silently. The repository's own code that odw would run is refused: .worktreeinclude symlink: lines link nothing, and a worktreeSetup the repository's own odw.config.json sets does not run (one from your own config does). A config inside the repository cannot loosen the trust your ~/.config/odw/config.json sets. An adapter's own "trust": "untrusted" makes it untrusted in every run. "trusted" (the default) changes nothing.
//agentEnv: ODW extension. "inherit" (the default) starts agent CLIs with ODW's whole environment. "minimal" passes only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, LANG, LC_*, TERM, TMPDIR, TZ (and the Windows system variables), the auth and config variables the built-in CLIs document (ANTHROPIC_*, CLAUDE_*, OPENAI_*, CODEX_*, GEMINI_*, GOOGLE_*, DASHSCOPE_*, QWEN_*, MOONSHOT_*, KIMI_*, CURSOR_*, OPENCODE_*, the proxy variables, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), the adapter's env, ODW_* and the names or globs in "agentEnvPass" (e.g. ["AWS_*"] for Claude Code on Bedrock).
//schemaKeywords: ODW extension. What happens to JSON Schema in an agent()'s schema that ODW's validator does not check. It checks type (one name), enum, properties, required, additionalProperties: false, items (one schema) and minItems; annotations such as description, title and format constrain nothing. Anything else (oneOf/anyOf/allOf, $ref, const, pattern, minimum, maxItems, type unions, …) is never silently unchecked: "warn" (the default) runs the call, validates the rest, and logs once per run which keywords, where, and who enforces them — an adapter whose CLI validates schemas itself ("flags.schema": the built-in claude, and codex for strict schemas), otherwise nobody; "strict" fails the call before it starts, naming each one. A malformed schema (a typo, an unknown type) fails in either mode. A CLI with flags.schema is handed every schema (claude --json-schema, codex --output-schema) and ODW still validates each reply. schemaPrompt "auto" describes the schema in the prompt only for a CLI that does not take it natively; "always" for every CLI.

//fallback.$comment: ODW extension: fallback chains. Rename "//fallback" to "fallback" to turn them on. When an agent's CLI has spent its usage quota or its login is refused (not a rate limit: that is retried in place, see transientRetries), the agent runs again on the next adapter listed for the one it was on — a fresh prompt, the same options, at the same permission tier (an adapter that cannot run that tier is skipped, with a log line) — and the run's log, odw status, the live view and the dashboard say where it went: "search:3 → claude after codex quota". An agent() call's own list, agent(prompt, { adapter: ["codex", "claude"] }), takes the place of these. Every adapter named must be configured.

//quotaBreaker: ODW extension. After this many quota failures in a row on one adapter, the run's later agents skip it — each starts on the next adapter of its fallback chain, or fails at once without one — and the run logs it once. 0 or null never skips an adapter.
//quotaWait: ODW extension: pause for a spent quota. Off (false) by default, since a run that silently waits for hours would surprise anyone who did not ask for it: an agent whose fallback chain is out of usage quota fails, as above. Set { "max": 21600 } (seconds) and the run waits instead — for the first of the chain's quotas to reset, when a CLI said when ("try again in 3h 22m", "resets 7pm", Claude's "usage limit reached|<epoch>") and that is at most max seconds away — then the agent starts over from its chain's start. It waits holding no slot, so agents on adapters with quota left keep running, and until the reset its CLI named the run passes over that adapter. odw status, odw list and the live view show "paused until 19:10 (codex quota)"; odw resume goes on at once and odw stop stops the run; with "paused" in notify.on the hooks fire once per pause. A quota failure that names no reset, or one past max, still fails the agent, and the log says why. The wait lives in the worker: if it dies, the run is stale and odw resume replays it.

//models.$comment: ODW extension: model tiers. Rename "//models" to "models" to turn them on. agent(prompt, { model: "@fast" }) — or a phase's model — runs each adapter with its own id for the tier: the one the agent runs on, or after a fallback the next one's. An adapter a tier names no model for runs its CLI's default (logged); an unknown tier fails the agent. A model without the @ is a model id, passed to every adapter as it is.

//expectRetries: ODW extension. agent(prompt, { expect }) states what must hold once the agent replied — some file changed or none (changes: true|false), files matching globs changed or created (files), a command exiting 0 in the agent's workspace (command, killed after timeout seconds, 600 by default), the reply matching a regular expression (match) — and odw checks it rather than asking the model; tool calls its CLI refused count as a miss too. Work that misses runs again with what it missed appended to its prompt, at most expectRetries times (an agent's own expectRetries overrides this); then it fails with reason unmet_expectation (permission when refused calls are among the misses) and the list of misses. Without any opt-in, an empty reply fails with reason empty_reply (allowEmpty: true accepts one).
//permissionDenials: ODW extension. What a reply that claims success does when its CLI refused the agent tool calls (claude's permission_denials, read through an adapter's output deniedPath; under the edit tier, Claude Code refuses every shell command that is not allowlisted): "warn" (the default) keeps the reply, records the refused calls as denied on the agent's agent_finished event and saved result, and logs one line; "fail" fails the agent with reason permission. An adapter's own "permissionDenials" overrides this; with expect, refused calls are a miss whatever it says.
//mcpFailures: ODW extension. Claude Code's stream-json starts with an init event listing the MCP servers it started the agent with and their status (read through an adapter's output mcpEvent and mcpPath). A server that is not "connected" is recorded as mcp on the agent's agent_finished or agent_failed event and saved result, and logged once per run for each server and status: "MCP server github failed to start (claude agent `fix-auth`): its tools were unavailable". "warn" (the default, as Claude Code itself only warns) keeps the reply; "fail" fails an agent whose server "failed" or "needs-auth" with reason mcp_unavailable. "pending" (still connecting in the background, or connected on first use) and "disabled" never fail it. agent(prompt, { expect: { mcp: ["github"] } }) instead makes a listed server that is not connected (or pending) a miss: retried, then unmet_expectation.
//agentLimits: ODW extension. What one agent may do before it is killed as a runaway: { "toolCalls", "costUsd", "outputTokens", "seconds", "repeat" } — tool calls over all its CLI runs, dollars and output tokens its CLIs reported, seconds since its first CLI run, and the same tool call (name + a hash of its arguments) "repeat" times in a row. Enforced live from claude, codex, kilo and opencode output; a breach kills the CLI and everything it started, and the agent fails with reason runaway and limitHit naming the limit and the evidence (Bash `npm test` ×5 in a row). An adapter's own "agentLimits" and agent(prompt, { limits }) override it key by key; null lifts one. {} (the default) sets none.
//orphanedBackground: ODW extension. In headless mode an agent can start a background shell command (Bash run_in_background) or subagent, end its turn, and exit: the work dies with the CLI while the result says success (anthropics/claude-code#85129). ODW reads the task events in Claude Code's stream-json (an adapter's output.background rules) and, when work is still running at the result event, records it as orphaned on the agent's agent_finished event and saved result and logs it once. "warn" (the default) keeps the reply; "fail" fails the agent with reason orphaned_background. With agent(prompt, { expect }) it is a miss: retried, then orphaned_background.
//questions: ODW extension. What an agent's question does: a clarifying tool call its CLI made (Claude Code's AskUserQuestion, read through an adapter's output.questions rules), which nobody can answer headless — the CLI returns an empty answer and the model goes on guessing (anthropics/claude-code#50728). ODW stops the CLI at the question, then: "checkpoint" (the default) asks a person at a checkpoint — odw approve <run> --checkpoint N --note "<answer>", the dashboard's card, notify's waiting hook (checkpoint.kind "question") — and runs the same call again, in the same worktree, its prompt told "earlier you asked X; the user answered Y" (odw reject fails it with reason needs_input); "fail" fails the agent with reason needs_input and its questions; "deny" runs the CLI without its question tool (an adapter's questionArgs: claude --disallowedTools AskUserQuestion) and tells the agent to assume and say so. An adapter's own "questions" and agent(prompt, { questions }) override it.
//redact: ODW extension. What odw keeps and serves of its agents — transcripts and stderr tails, saved results, events (log lines, agent and exec() failures), the run's error, webhook payloads — has its likely secrets replaced by «redacted:<kind>» before it is written, and is marked redacted: true. env: the value (8 characters or more) of every variable whose name looks secret (*_KEY, *TOKEN, *SECRET*, *PASSWORD*, AUTHORIZATION, cloud credentials) in the environment odw starts agents and commands with — its own and each adapter's env — wherever it appears, and the value of any NAME=value printed whose NAME looks secret (a .env file, env output). patterns: well-known token shapes (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Slack, AWS, Google keys, JWTs, private-key blocks, Bearer tokens). extra: more regular expressions (JavaScript sources). The run's result is the workflow's own data: only patterns and extra apply to it. Prompts and what agents see are never redacted, nor kept diffs (they are what odw apply applies). false keeps everything as printed; odw doctor says which.

//notify.$comment: ODW extension: run-end hooks. Rename "//notify" to "notify" to turn them on. They fire once, after the run's final state is written, and can never change it; a failing or slow hook is only logged to the run's worker.log. command: an argv run WITHOUT a shell (killed after 30s), with ODW_RUN_ID, ODW_RUN_STATE, ODW_WORKFLOW, ODW_RUN_DIR, ODW_RESULT_FILE (only when the run has a result), ODW_DURATION_SEC, ODW_AGENTS and ODW_FAILED_AGENTS in its environment. webhook: an http(s) URL that receives a JSON POST (10s limit) whose text/content fields render as-is in Slack and Discord. on: which final states fire them (default: all three) — and, opt-in, "waiting" (a checkpoint() waits for a person) and "paused" (the run pauses for a spent quota, see quotaWait).

//otel.$comment: ODW extension: OpenTelemetry export. Rename "//otel" to "otel" to turn it on (true works too); the OTEL_* variables alone never do. Once a run ended, the worker posts its trace — invoke_workflow, phase, invoke_agent and execute_tool spans after the GenAI semantic conventions, with usage, cost, retries and fallbacks — once, as OTLP/HTTP JSON to endpoint + /v1/traces (5s limit; a failure is one line in the run's worker.log and never changes the run). endpoint: the receiver's base URL; omitted, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, else http://localhost:4318. headers: sent with it, over OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS; their values are secrets — never logged or shown. captureContent: also export replies, tool input and output and error text (redacted, each cut at 4096 characters); OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true does the same. odw export <run> --otlp writes any run's trace.

codex.label: Codex CLI
codex.untrustedNote: codex has no documented way to ignore the repository's AGENTS.md — its instructions still reach the agent (its .codex/ config, hooks and rules load only if you trusted the project in your own Codex config)

gemini.label: Gemini CLI
gemini.untrustedNote: gemini has no documented way to ignore the repository's GEMINI.md and .gemini/settings.json when headless — its instructions, MCP servers and hooks still reach the agent

kimi.label: Kimi CLI
kimi.untrustedNote: kimi has no documented way to ignore the repository's AGENTS.md and skills — they still reach the agent

omp.label: Oh My Pi
omp.untrustedNote: omp keeps the repository's extensions, skills and rules out (--no-extensions --no-skills --no-rules), but has no documented way to ignore its AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, hooks or MCP config — they still reach the agent

kilo.label: Kilo Code
kilo.untrustedNote: kilo has no documented way to ignore the repository's AGENTS.md, kilo.json and .kilo/ agents, commands and plugins — they still reach the agent

opencode.label: OpenCode
opencode.untrustedNote: opencode has no documented way to ignore the repository's AGENTS.md, opencode.json and .opencode/ agents, commands and plugins — they still reach the agent

cursor.label: Cursor Agent CLI
cursor.untrustedNote: cursor has no documented way to ignore the repository's .cursor/rules, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, mcp.json and hooks — headless it runs only on a workspace it trusts, and they still reach the agent

agy.label: Antigravity CLI
agy.untrustedNote: agy has no documented way to ignore the repository's AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and .agents/ rules, skills, agents and MCP servers — they still reach the agent
